What we paint

Room by room, or the whole house

Most interiors we do in occupied homes. We work around your life, not the other way round.

Walls & ceilings

Patched, sanded, primed where needed and rolled to a consistent sheen — including the ceiling everyone else charges extra to touch.

Trim, baseboards & crown

Caulked, filled and cut in by hand. The line between wall and trim is where amateur work shows immediately.

Doors & casings

Sprayed off their hinges wherever we can, for a hard finish with no brush marks.

Stairwells & high ceilings

Two-story foyers and open stairwells, staged and scaffolded properly rather than balanced off a ladder.

Drywall & plaster repair

Nail pops, settling cracks, water stains and old Pittsburgh plaster patched and blended before a drop of color goes on.

Accent walls & feature finishes

Color blocking, wainscot, board and batten, and trim details that make a plain room look intentional.

How we work inside your house

You should barely notice we’re here

The complaint homeowners have about interior painters is almost never the paint. It’s the mess, the dust, and the not knowing when anyone is showing up.

  • Protect first

    Floors covered wall to wall, furniture moved to the center and wrapped, fixtures and hardware removed rather than taped around.

  • Repair and prep

    Every crack, nail pop and dent filled, sanded and spot‑primed. Sanding is vacuum‑assisted so the dust doesn’t end up in your kitchen.

  • Cut and coat

    Lines cut by hand, two coats rolled, sheen consistent across the whole wall. Trim and doors sprayed where practical.

  • Reset the room

    Hardware back on, furniture back in place, floors vacuumed. Every day, not just on the last day.

Winter is the smart window

Book interiors off-season

Exteriors stop when it gets cold. Interiors, cabinets and basements don’t — which means November through March is when you get the most flexible scheduling of the year.

Interior FAQ

The practical questions

A standard bedroom with walls, ceiling and trim typically runs $450 to $900. Open‑plan living areas, two‑story foyers and rooms needing significant plaster repair cost more. Whole‑house interiors are almost always better value per room than doing one at a time.

No. We work in occupied homes constantly. We stage room by room so you always have somewhere to live, and everything gets put back each evening.

Modern waterborne acrylics are far milder than the oil‑based paints people remember. We can spec low‑VOC or zero‑VOC products if you have young children, pets or anyone sensitive in the house — just tell us at the walk‑through.

Yes, and it’s free. Colors behave completely differently under Pittsburgh’s grey winter light than they do on a chip in a showroom. We’ll bring large samples, put them on your actual walls and look at them at different times of day.

Yes. Older Pittsburgh homes settle and the plaster cracks — it’s normal. We cut out, tape and blend structural cracks rather than skimming over them, so they don’t reappear through the new paint in a year.
